test.name: Calendar-history question must not trigger a convert-dates conversion
test.description: User asks WHY a calendar convention existed (the history of Quaker numbered months), not for a specific date conversion. convert-dates performs mechanical calendar-system conversions; it must NOT perform one on a why-did-this-exist question. The router often answers such history questions directly, or routes to historical-context; either is acceptable so long as convert-dates does not butt in with a conversion.

input.user_message: Why did Quakers use numbered months instead of named months? What's the history of that convention?

negative.explanation: The user wants the cultural/religious history of the numbered-month convention, not a date conversion. Ideally the router picks historical-context, but in practice it frequently answers the history directly with no skill invoked (invoked=[]) — an acceptable no-harm outcome. convert-dates is never invoked here and has no leverage over that routing decision, so requiring historical-context to fire is really a historical-context triggering assertion, not something this convert-dates test can control (tracked separately as a routing-negative issue alongside ut_historical_context_009). The routing-independent invariant this test actually enforces is the convert-dates-scoped one: convert-dates must NOT perform a calendar conversion on a history question, gated deterministically by the tag-gated validator test_no_spurious_conversion (eval/harness/validators/test_convert_dates.py, no-spurious-conversion tag), which fails the run if convert_calendar is invoked. NOTE: this intentionally drops the original 'must route to historical-context' assertion — that belongs to historical-context's description/triggering, not to a convert-dates test.

judge_context: convert-dates should NOT perform a calendar conversion — this is a history question, not a date to convert
Answering the history directly, or routing to historical-context, are both acceptable
Should NOT introduce any Julian or Gregorian shift
